questions.q: Why does the summary say starting with a single push-up works?
a: Getting started creates momentum for more
One push-up builds strength faster than many
It removes the need for any workout plan
It burns more fat than a full training session
questions.why: Lesson 1 applies Newton's first law: once you begin, adding a few more reps feels easy.

questions.q: What does the summary say is a more reliable driver of habits than motivation?
a: Willpower
Inspiration
Accountability partners
Rewards
questions.why: The overview says motivation is unreliable, so the book builds its strategy on willpower.

questions.q: What does the summary call the most important part of tracking habits?
a: Checking the tracker daily and noting progress
Choosing an app with a large community
Recording only the days you succeed
Setting a brand new goal each week
questions.why: Lesson 2 says looking at the tracker every day keeps progress visible and reminds you to finish.

questions.q: What does the summary advise after you greatly exceed a mini habit goal?
a: Treat it as a bonus and keep the standard small
Raise the goal to match your best day
Add a second habit straight away
Pause the habit until motivation returns
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns that raising the bar after a record day is a trap that leads to falling off.

questions.q: What does the summary say it means when a mini habit starts to feel boring?
a: It has become a real habit
It is time to choose a harder goal
It has stopped being useful
You need a different reward
questions.why: Lesson 3 says boredom signals that the behavior has settled into a habit, which is worth celebrating.
